ceramic.name: kärl, Lerkärl
ceramic.title: kärl, Lerkärl
ceramic.reason: Blackware carved pottery vessel by Madeline Naranjo of Santa Clara Pueblo, signed on the base — Santa Clara is a Tewa-speaking pueblo, so this is a directly attributed Tewa ceramic.

ceramic.name: kärl, skål, Lerskål
ceramic.title: kärl, skål, Lerskål
ceramic.reason: A polychrome earthenware bowl with classic Tewa/Hano (Hopi-Tewa) painted design in brown and red on a cream slip, consistent with Pueblo pottery from Arizona attributed to the Tewa people at Hano. The shape, slip, and geometric/curvilinear motifs match traditional Tewa ceramic work.

ceramic.name: kärl, skål
ceramic.title: kärl, skål
ceramic.reason: A hand-painted polychrome pottery bowl attributed to Tewa/Hano potters of Arizona, with typical geometric Hopi-Tewa style decoration — a classic form of Puebloan ceramic art made by this people.

jewelry.name: regalia; back-ornament; medallion
jewelry.title: regalia; back-ornament (upper); medallion
jewelry.reason: A beaded bustle medallion with feather back-ornament used in Plains-style dance regalia; such beadwork and bustle ornaments are made and worn across Pueblo peoples including the Tewa, so this fits the claimed culture's material culture.

jewelry.name: regalia; choker
jewelry.title: regalia; choker
jewelry.reason: This is a loom-beaded choker with a classic Plains-style geometric diamond pattern, made as part of contemporary powwow regalia. Beaded powwow regalia of this type is a widely practiced Native American craft form and plausible for a Tewa maker/wearer; nothing in the image contradicts the claim.

jewelry.name: regalia; arm-band
jewelry.title: regalia; arm-band
jewelry.reason: The image shows a pair of loom-beaded armbands with a geometric diamond design, hide backing, and ties — a type of beadwork worn as part of contemporary powwow regalia. Such beadwork is made and worn by many Native American people, including Pueblo peoples like the Tewa, so it is plausible for the claimed group even though the design style is widely shared.

masks-ritual.name: regalia; arm-ornament
masks-ritual.title: regalia; arm-ornament (bustles)
masks-ritual.reason: The image shows a pair of feathered arm bustles (dance regalia) with mirrored, sequinned centers — a type of ceremonial ornament used in Pueblo social dances, consistent with Tewa (Rio Grande Pueblo) use, though not distinguishable from other Pueblo peoples' regalia.

garment.name: regalia; belt
garment.title: regalia; belt
garment.reason: The image shows a loom-beaded leather belt with classic diamond/feather motifs, part of powwow regalia — this is a style of beadwork worn by many Native American groups, including Pueblo peoples like the Tewa at intertribal powwows, so it is plausible for the claimed people even though the design itself isn't diagnostic of Tewa specifically.

garment.name: regalia; legging
garment.title: regalia; legging
garment.reason: These are goat-hide/angora powwow dance leggings, a type of regalia worn by many Native American dancers including Pueblo peoples such as the Tewa; nothing here contradicts the Tewa attribution.

garment.name: regalia; moccasin
garment.title: regalia; moccasin
garment.reason: A pair of hide moccasins with lazy-stitch beadwork in a diamond/lane pattern — this is a documented type of footwear worn by Native American peoples including the Tewa, and nothing here points to another specific culture.

garment.name: regalia; bandolier
garment.title: regalia; bandolier
garment.reason: A hand-loomed glass-beadwork bandolier with hide fringe and mirror disks, part of a powwow regalia ensemble — a plausible Native American dance accessory; nothing in the image contradicts a Tewa (Pueblo) maker, and Pueblo people commonly participate in powwow culture.
